biography: Finlay Hutchison's journey began not on a racetrack, but on the windswept coast of Scotland, where he spent his youth tinkering with go-karts in his father’s garage. His raw talent became evident at the age of 16, when he won the Scottish Junior Karting Championship against seasoned competitors. A defining moment came during a Formula Ford race at Knockhill, where, despite a mechanical failure in the final lap, Hutchison managed to nurse his car across the finish line to secure a podium finish. This gritty determination caught the eye of Mercedes-AMG, leading to his current position within their development program. Despite flashes of brilliance, inconsistency has plagued his ascent, leaving many wondering if he can harness his potential and become a true force in motorsport. Currently, he is focused on proving his worth to the team and securing a more permanent role within their GT racing program.
drivingStyle: Hutchison's driving style can be described as a controlled aggression. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum speed from the car during qualifying, often pushing the limits of grip. However, in race conditions, this aggressive approach sometimes translates into overdriving, leading to tire degradation and costly mistakes. He excels in wet conditions, demonstrating exceptional car control and a willingness to take risks, but needs to improve his consistency and racecraft in dry races.

rivalries.reason: A clash on track at Spa during a GT World Challenge race resulted in both drivers retiring. Hutchison felt Bellini was overly aggressive, while Bellini accused Hutchison of blocking.
Dubois and Hutchison were teammates early in their careers, and a fierce competition to be the top driver within the team created a tense and sometimes acrimonious relationship.
Tanaka consistently outperforms Hutchison in long-distance races due to his superior tire management skills, a constant source of frustration for the young Brit.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Refuses to eat anything green the day before a race, believing it brings bad luck.
Listens to bagpipe music to calm his nerves before entering the car.
famousQuote: Sometimes you have to send it. It’s all or nothing. Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 GT World Challenge Europe Sprint Cup race at Brands Hatch, after a daring overtake on the last lap, marking his first major international victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Spa in 2023, due to a self-admitted lapse in concentration, costing his team a potential victory and causing significant damage to the car.
